title: LC2K Cache Simulator
summary: A cache simulator I built in C to follow what happens on each memory access.
overview: I built this simulator in C to explore how a cache handles memory reads and writes. It connects to an LC-2K processor simulator and supports different cache sizes and organizations, so I could compare how those choices affect memory access.
The project covers cache hits, misses, replacement, and writing modified data back to memory. I tested those behaviors with small programs that made each kind of memory access easy to follow.

title: Autonomous MBots
summary: Research work on how mobile robots move, and how to make that behavior safer.
overview: My work with MBots focused on motion analysis and real-time safety. I used wheel encoder data to examine velocity and acceleration, and plotted the results to understand how the robots behaved over time.
This was part of my research work in the MARVL Lab. I helped with safety protocols and the tools used to inspect and discuss robot motion.

title: This website
summary: A home for my projects, and a project of its own.
overview: I built this site as a place for my projects and work history. It uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a small Python build script that combines shared templates and project content into static pages.

I’ve focused on making it comfortable to use on phones and desktops, with keyboard navigation, light and dark themes, and readable pages even without JavaScript. Browser checks cover the layouts, preferences, contact form, and common accessibility issues.

title: Handwritten Character Recognition
summary: Comparing two kinds of neural networks on handwritten English characters.
overview: For this project, I compared feedforward and convolutional neural networks on handwritten English characters using Julia. I trained the models with the handwritten character dataset by Cohen, Afshar, Tapson, and van Schaik.
I looked at accuracy, confusion matrices, and learning curves to understand which characters each model recognized well and where it struggled.

title: 3D Mapping from LiDAR Data
summary: Using Julia to bring separate LiDAR scans together into a 3D map.
overview: I used Julia to combine separate LiDAR scans into a 3D map. Each scan captured the scene from a different position, so the project involved processing the point clouds and aligning them in a shared coordinate frame.
The resulting visualization let me inspect how the scans fit together and spot problems in the alignment.

title: Orbital Satellite Simulation
summary: Using a ground robot to study aspects of satellite motion.
overview: In the VODCA Lab, I helped develop a satellite orbit simulation using an omnidirectional ground rover as a physical testbed. My work connected orbital models to robot commands and supported real-time data collection and analysis.
The rover provided a way to study aspects of orbital motion in a lab, within the limits of what a ground robot can represent.

title: Auction Notification System
summary: A Python tool that watches auction listings and sends alerts for matching items.
overview: I built this Python tool to keep track of online auctions without repeatedly checking listings by hand. It collects listings, filters them by details such as keywords and price, and sends a notification when an item matches.
The project brought together web scraping, APIs, and an alert workflow, with retries and rate limiting to handle changes in the listing sources.

title: Indie Game Development
summary: A Unity project where I’ve worked on gameplay, levels, and game assets.
overview: This is a solo game project in Unity. I’ve worked on movement, combat, and interaction in C#, along with levels, Blender assets, and player feedback through UI and audio.
It gives me a place to try gameplay ideas and work on the different pieces that make a game feel playable. Reusable scenes and components help keep those experiments manageable.

title: Quadplane Development
summary: Working on an aircraft that combines vertical takeoff with fixed-wing flight.
overview: I worked on a hybrid aircraft that combines a quadcopter’s vertical takeoff with fixed-wing flight. The project involved flight-control logic, hardware integration, and testing how the aircraft behaved in different operating modes.
I was especially interested in the transition between hovering and forward flight, where the controls have to account for two very different ways of flying.
